name: Minimum squared max-to-min pair-distance ratio for 12 planar points

parameters.objective: maximum squared pair distance divided by minimum squared pair distance

source_review.definition: Twelve arbitrary distinct rational points in the plane minimize maximum squared pair distance divided by minimum squared pair distance. No collinearity or bounding-box constraint. Density and continuity preserve the real-coordinate infimum.
source_review.primary_source: Friedman maxmin n12 page attributes Rechenberg2006 value5+2sqrt3 without optimality proof. Root read the source diagram and independently reconstructed Q(sqrt3) coordinates: all66 pairs have minimum squared distance1 and maximum5+2sqrt3, with21 minimum pairs. Exact rational approximation to sqrt3 yields the formally reproduced slightly weaker ratio; it is not identified with the exact irrational record.
source_review.independent_method: For each of five saved witnesses, rebuild all66 distances via the rational Gram identity norm(i)+norm(j)-2dot(i,j), separate from formal coordinate differences, and divide exact maximum by positive minimum.
source_review.open_status: AlphaEvolve2511.02864v1 section6.50 distinguishes proved n<=8 from numerical n9..30 candidates. Later improvements at16/21/22/29 do not settle12; no n12 optimality proof located in reviewed sources.
